tasks.short: Explain Noordhaven’s financial results and the issues management needs to act on.

today.trigger: The monthly reporting deadline or a management request for an update.
steps: Gather AFAS figures, the nightly Power BI extract and the approved budget.
Reconcile totals and investigate changes with colleagues at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Build Excel tables and write explanations of the main movements.
Review the report with the Controller and present management’s actions.
drudgery: Checking which extract and budget version were used
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: reconciling different reporting snapshots and chasing explanations. Validate the baseline before treating the saving as measured.

lenses.faster: Automated tables remove copying, and a model drafts commentary from reconciled figures and supplied explanations. For each 60 minutes today, allow 27 minutes for investigating movements, checking the draft and discussing actions: 55% saved.
lenses.autonomous: An approved reporting snapshot starts the workflow; calculations run and commentary is drafted with source references. The Accountant approves the explanations before the Controller releases the report.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each site manager a weekly margin briefing that separates volume, agency labour and other cost movements. Demand would probably grow as preparation becomes cheaper, provided managers can act on the findings.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the same tables or polishing standard paragraphs. The Accountant gets more time to understand operational causes and discuss corrective action.
lenses.options: Compare explanations based on volume, rate and labour mix before choosing the management narrative. These alternatives can change whether management adjusts staffing, pricing or spending.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards investigating exceptions and discussing site performance. With delegated authority, the Accountant selects issues for management escalation and requests supporting explanations; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst’s first pass at site budget variance explanations after learning operational drivers, forecasting definitions and the approved budget model.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant distinguishes a convincing explanation from a numerical coincidence and knows when site context changes the management message.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: a fixed workflow supplies reconciled tables and verified operational explanations to one commentary draft; unpredictable agent exploration is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: The Controller marks a dated AFAS reporting snapshot ready.
steps: Calculate variances and reconcile report totals using versioned rules.
Collect site explanations through a standard form and flag missing responses.
Draft commentary using only approved figures and supplied explanations, with references.
Route the report to the Accountant for factual review and then to the Controller for release.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves every report’s explanations; the Controller approves management release.
data_needed: Dated actuals, budget and prior-period figures
Account-to-site and reporting mappings
Materiality thresholds
Site explanations and report access permissions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint reporting folder containing the snapshot ID, calculations, source references, draft changes and approvals.

evidence.claim: A field study reported faster closes among accountants using AI, but does not establish Noordhaven’s report preparation saving.
Deterministic variance calculations and a constrained commentary draft are technically feasible; the proposed workflow and percentage remain estimates.

risks: The nightly Power BI extract may lag adjustments posted in AFAS.
A fluent draft may invent a cause that site evidence does not support.
Payroll detail could expose personal information unnecessarily; use aggregated site costs.
research_questions: Can reporting totals be reconciled automatically to a dated AFAS snapshot?
How much reporting time currently goes into formatting versus investigating causes?
Do site managers supply explanations that are specific enough to support useful commentary?

tasks.short: Prepare and check Noordhaven’s VAT and corporate tax returns.

today.trigger: A VAT filing deadline, corporate tax deadline or revised assessment.
steps: Collect AFAS tax balances, transaction details and supporting documents.
Reconcile tax accounts and check classifications, including cross-border and reverse-charge transactions.
Calculate the return and document adjustments or estimates.
Obtain approval, submit through the authorised route and arrange the approved payment.
drudgery: Collecting supporting documents for recurring checks
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: resolving inconsistent tax codes and supporting estimates. VAT and corporate tax effort must be measured separately.

lenses.faster: Rules calculate routine amounts and assemble reconciliation schedules; Jonas can assist checks if Noordhaven has the required AFAS version and tax functionality. For each 60 minutes today, retain 33 minutes for exceptions, estimates, approval and filing: 45% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A filing-calendar event starts extraction, reconciliation and draft preparation. Every return and tax estimate requires human approval before submission, with payment authorised separately.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: decide each month whether Noordhaven’s expected tax cash requirement needs revising. Demand would grow as updates become cheaper because Treasury and Finance need earlier visibility of payment peaks.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding familiar reconciliation schedules. The Accountant gets more time to resolve difficult tax treatment and prevent recurring coding errors.
lenses.options: Compare supported treatments for disputed deductions or timing differences, showing both cash effects and uncertainty. This changes which position is approved and whether external tax advice is needed.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from arithmetic towards managing tax exceptions and maintaining an evidence-backed filing calendar. The Accountant can resolve routine coding within approved policy, while estimates and novel positions remain with the Finance Director or tax adviser; expertise increases.
reach: Absorb the Bookkeeper’s review of recurring VAT-code exceptions after learning Noordhaven’s tax-code mapping and cross-border transaction rules.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant assesses whether transaction substance supports the tax treatment and recognises when a legal interpretation needs specialist advice.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: repeatable calculations and reconciliations use explicit tax rules; contextual AI assistance supports review without determining amounts or submitting returns.

in_practice.trigger: The filing calendar opens a return period after its AFAS records are ready.
steps: Extract tax-coded transactions and reconcile them to the general ledger.
Apply approved calculations and flag unusual codes, missing evidence and cross-border exceptions.
Prepare the draft return and supporting schedules; use Jonas assistance if available.
Route exceptions and all estimates to the Accountant and designated tax approver.
After approval, submit through the authorised channel and create a separately approved payment request.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant checks each return; the designated tax approver signs off estimates and positions before filing. Rabobank payment approval remains separate.
systems: AFAS tax functionality and Jonas, if licensed and available
data_needed: Tax codes, transactions and tax-account balances
Prior returns and approved tax positions
Supporting invoices and cross-border evidence
Current tax rules, filing dates and authorisation matrix
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint tax file with reproducible calculations, exception resolutions, return versions, approval and submission receipts.

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas supports tax-return assistance from Profit 8, including VAT from 2026, and leaves checking responsibility with the user.
The digest’s governance source identifies tax estimates as requiring human review.

risks: Incorrect tax-code mappings can systematically misstate a return.
Jonas availability in AFAS does not establish that Noordhaven has the relevant tax module or configuration.
An estimate or unusual VAT treatment may require an external Dutch tax specialist.
A draft must never bypass filing or payment authorisation.
research_questions: Which AFAS version, tax modules and Jonas features are actually available to Noordhaven?
What proportion of effort is routine VAT calculation versus corporate tax judgement?
Can every return total be traced back to transactions and approved adjustments?
Who is authorised to approve estimates, submit returns and release payments?

tasks.short: Check balance sheet balances and explain movements in assets, liabilities, income and costs.

today.trigger: The month-close timetable or an unusual balance movement.
steps: Gather AFAS balances, bank statements and supporting asset, receivable and payable schedules.
Reconcile schedules to ledger accounts and compare with prior periods.
Investigate missing support, unusual movements and valuation questions.
Prepare proposed corrections and obtain approval for adjustments.
drudgery: Matching schedule totals to ledger balances
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: assembling evidence and repeatedly resolving mismatches across schedules and ledger snapshots.

lenses.faster: Rule-based tie-outs and movement calculations disappear from manual work; a model turns the resulting exceptions and evidence into a draft workpaper. For each 60 minutes today, retain 24 minutes for valuation judgement, evidence checks and adjustment review: 60% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A frozen close snapshot starts reconciliation and workpaper drafting. The Accountant approves each completed account review and any proposed adjustment before it counts as closed.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: decide weekly whether overdue receivables warrant a provision review. Demand would grow as screening becomes cheaper, because credit deterioration can be addressed before month end.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting for attachments and recalculating familiar movements. The Accountant spends more time investigating balances that could materially misstate the accounts.
lenses.options: Compare documented provision and asset-life scenarios against the approved accounting policy. The alternatives can change the proposed adjustment and whether the Controller seeks more evidence.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards resolving valuation and completeness exceptions across the three sites. The Accountant can clear reconciliations within delegated thresholds and recommend adjustments, while material valuation approval stays with the Controller; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Credit and Collections Officer’s preparation of receivables evidence for provision reviews after learning ageing definitions, dispute status and collection histories.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant recognises when a balance ties mathematically but remains incomplete, unsupported or economically implausible.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: deterministic checks produce the numbers, and one constrained model call drafts a referenced account-review workpaper for a mandatory tie-out gate.

in_practice.trigger: A close snapshot and its supporting schedules are marked ready.
steps: Reconcile each schedule to its AFAS control account and calculate movements.
Flag unsupported balances, stale items and breaches of agreed thresholds.
Draft a workpaper from calculated results and linked evidence, leaving unsupported explanations blank.
Have the Accountant resolve exceptions and approve the account review and proposed corrections.
in_practice.human_gate: Each workpaper requires an Accountant’s tie-out and evidence approval; adjusting entries follow the existing posting authorisation.
data_needed: General ledger balances and transactions
Asset, receivables and payables schedules
Bank statements and supporting documents
Accounting policies, thresholds and prior approved reviews
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close file with snapshot IDs, reconciliation results, linked evidence, unresolved items and approvals.

evidence.claim: A vendor-run benchmark demonstrated strong model performance on bounded month-end scenarios, while excluding important contextual and communication work.
The broader accounting benchmark shows continuing failures in judgement and multi-step reasoning, supporting a mandatory workpaper review.

risks: A mathematically reconciled schedule may omit transactions or use the wrong period.
A model may add an undocumented valuation assumption.
Savings depend on usable schedules and reliable document links.
US accounting benchmarks do not validate Dutch GAAP workpapers.
research_questions: Which balance sheet accounts have reliable supporting schedules and stable reconciliation rules?
Can reviewers rebuild each workpaper from the saved inputs without relying on model reasoning?
How often do valuation judgements dominate the work rather than basic tie-outs?

tasks.short: Write clear audit findings with evidence, financial impact and agreed follow-up.

today.trigger: An internal control review or external audit identifies a possible finding.
steps: Gather test results, documents and explanations from the process owner.
Confirm what happened, its scope and the financial or control impact.
Write the finding, evidence references and proposed action.
Discuss wording and ownership, then obtain approval and record follow-up.
drudgery: Reformatting findings into the audit template
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: assembling references and reconciling draft wording with evidence and process-owner responses.

lenses.faster: A model assembles a first draft and evidence index from an approved finding packet. For each 60 minutes today, retain 27 minutes for checking support, deciding severity and agreeing action: 55% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A completed testing packet starts the draft; the workflow identifies missing support and prepares the finding. The Accountant approves the content before the Controller authorises release to the process owner or auditor.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give each site manager a monthly briefing on unresolved control weaknesses and the evidence needed to close them. Demand would grow as preparation becomes cheaper, provided it improves follow-up rather than adding meetings.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss formatting evidence lists and merging tracked changes. The Accountant gets more time for difficult conversations about why a control failed and what will fix it.
lenses.options: Compare remediation choices such as an access restriction, an extra approval or an automated reconciliation. Showing cost and coverage changes which control management chooses.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards evaluating severity and negotiating practical remedies. The Accountant gains delegated authority to request evidence and verify remediation, while management accepts residual risk; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller’s preparation of the audit action tracker and closure evidence after learning severity definitions, escalation thresholds and audit evidence standards.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant judges whether evidence justifies an allegation, hears the process owner fairly and makes recommendations that people can actually implement.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: one bounded transformation converts a structured evidence packet into a report draft; severity, conclusions and release remain human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: The Accountant marks an evidence packet complete enough for drafting.
steps: Validate that the packet includes the tested population, exceptions and source documents.
Draft the finding, impact and proposed actions with references to supplied evidence.
Flag claims without support and separate process-owner explanations from verified facts.
Review severity and wording with the Accountant, record the owner’s response and approve release.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant verifies every factual claim and proposed finding; the Controller approves formal release and escalation.
data_needed: Test definitions, population and exception results
Source documents and verified explanations
Finding template and severity criteria
Process-owner responses and action responsibilities
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint audit file with evidence references, draft history, review decisions, owner responses and approved actions.

evidence.claim: Models can struggle with judgement and reasoning across accounting files, so generated findings require source verification.
Drafting a report from a constrained evidence packet is feasible, but the digest provides no validated Dutch statutory audit-file result.

risks: A draft could overstate severity or imply misconduct without sufficient evidence.
Incomplete testing populations can produce misleading conclusions.
Audit packets may contain confidential financial or employee information.
Agreed wording can obscure a real issue unless the reviewer preserves the evidence.
research_questions: Are findings supported by structured testing packets or mostly informal notes?
How much report time is drafting versus severity assessment and negotiation?
Can the system preserve exact references and distinguish verified facts from interview statements?

tasks.short: Assess Noordhaven’s tax positions, including financing, asset values and depreciation.

today.trigger: A financing change, investment, valuation question or tax provision update.
steps: Collect Noordhaven’s contracts, asset schedules and relevant financial balances.
Identify the tax question and applicable Dutch treatment.
Calculate financing, valuation or depreciation effects and compare supported treatments.
Document assumptions and obtain approval or external tax advice.
drudgery: Maintaining several versions of tax assumptions
today.time_sinks: This O*NET statement is interpreted as assessing Noordhaven’s own tax positions, not examining other taxpayers. The actual mix of financing, asset and valuation work needs confirmation.

lenses.faster: A copilot extracts candidate contract terms and drafts a comparison while approved spreadsheets calculate the effects. For each 60 minutes today, retain 39 minutes for validating terms, interpreting Dutch tax rules and obtaining approval: 35% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A new contract or provision-review request creates a checklist and draft analysis. The Accountant directs the work, verifies every assumption and obtains approval before the position affects a provision or return.
lenses.ambitious: New service: offer Operations a tax-impact review before approving major forklift, vehicle or warehouse equipment investments. Demand would grow as review becomes cheaper because more investment options could be assessed before commitment.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping financing terms or repairing duplicated spreadsheets. The Accountant gets more time to understand commercial substance and discuss investment choices.
lenses.options: Compare purchase, lease and financing proposals using supported tax and cash assumptions. The scenarios can change the selected investment structure, subject to operational needs and specialist advice.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards advising on proposed transactions before they are signed. The Accountant gains authority to request a tax review and recommend a treatment, while the Finance Director approves material positions; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst’s preparation of tax-sensitive investment cash-flow scenarios after learning capital budgeting, lease terms and the boundary between accounting and tax treatment.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant recognises the substance of a transaction, challenges assumptions and knows when uncertainty requires a Dutch tax specialist.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: the relevant tax question and evidence vary by transaction, and the person must lead interpretation; approved calculation models provide the arithmetic.

in_practice.trigger: The Accountant opens a review for a proposed transaction or changed tax estimate.
steps: Use the copilot to extract candidate terms with page references from approved documents.
Have the Accountant verify terms and define the tax questions and permissible assumptions.
Calculate scenarios in a versioned spreadsheet and draft an assumption register.
Review the proposed position with the Finance Director or tax adviser and record the approved treatment.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant validates inputs and interpretation; material positions and every tax estimate require the designated human approver.
data_needed: Financing and investment contracts
Asset values and depreciation schedules
Approved calculation models
Current Dutch tax references and prior approved positions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint tax-position file with verified terms, model versions, scenarios, assumptions and approval.

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas provides contextual assistance for corporate tax returns; this does not prove autonomous valuation or transaction advice.
The broader accounting benchmark identifies judgement and multi-step reasoning as continuing weaknesses.

risks: US accounting performance does not establish competence in Dutch tax law.
An extracted contract term may omit a condition that changes the treatment.
Accounting values and tax values may differ.
This task may occupy much less time at Noordhaven than the O*NET allocation suggests.
research_questions: Which tax-position questions do Noordhaven’s Accountants actually handle rather than outsource?
Are existing calculation models approved, reproducible and maintained?
Can document extraction capture conditions as well as headline rates and dates?
Would earlier tax reviews materially change investment decisions?

tasks.short: Check finance systems and recommend controls that keep records reliable.

today.trigger: A control review, system change, reconciliation failure or audit recommendation.
steps: Map the relevant AFAS, bank, agency portal and reporting data flow.
Inspect permissions, interfaces and reconciliations with system owners.
Test transactions and investigate failures with process owners.
Compare control improvements and recommend an implementation plan.
Verify that the approved change addresses the weakness.
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: locating system evidence and separating genuine control failures from configuration or data-quality problems.

lenses.faster: Reusable tests remove repeated comparisons, and a copilot organises evidence and drafts control alternatives. For each 60 minutes today, retain 39 minutes for walkthroughs, design judgement, consultation and verification: 35% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A system change or scheduled review refreshes permission comparisons and interface tests automatically. The Accountant leads diagnosis and approves recommendations; authorised system owners implement changes.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: decide after each finance-system configuration change whether affected controls need retesting. Demand would grow as checks become cheaper because smaller changes could receive proportionate review.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss comparing nearly identical exports by hand. The Accountant gets more time to understand failure paths and design controls that fit shift operations.
lenses.options: Compare preventive access controls, transaction validation and detective reconciliations against the same failure scenario. This changes the chosen balance between operational friction and financial exposure.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards assessing how system changes affect financial reliability. With delegation, the Accountant signs off financial control test results and escalates failed changes, while IT retains access administration; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller’s maintenance of finance control-test specifications after learning AFAS authorisation, interface design and change management.
Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst’s payroll-to-ledger interface reconciliation after learning payroll mappings, access boundaries and reconciliation ownership.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant connects technical weaknesses to real financial consequences and judges whether a proposed control is workable for site teams.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: system assessment and control design require person-led investigation; deterministic tests and drafting assistance support that work.

in_practice.trigger: An approved change ticket or scheduled control review identifies the systems in scope.
steps: Collect read-only configuration, permission and interface evidence.
Run versioned tests for reconciliation failures, conflicting permissions and incomplete transfers.
Have the Accountant investigate exceptions with system and process owners.
Use the copilot to compare control alternatives against the confirmed failure modes.
Obtain change approval and rerun the affected tests after implementation.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves findings and financial control conclusions; system owners approve and implement configuration or access changes.
data_needed: System and interface inventory
Permission exports and segregation-of-duties matrix
Control totals, refresh records and change tickets
Approved test definitions and exception history
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint control register with test versions, input dates, failures, recommendations, change approvals and retest results.

evidence.claim: Deterministic permission and interface tests are feasible when configuration exports and control definitions are available.
Accounting benchmarks show continuing reasoning failures, supporting person-led control assessment rather than autonomous system redesign.

risks: Unavailable or incomplete configuration exports can create false assurance.
A permission conflict is a risk indicator, not proof that misuse occurred.
System changes may solve one issue while disrupting a site or payroll interface.
Employee-level monitoring requires AVG assessment and consultation with the OR where applicable.
research_questions: Can each system provide complete permission and interface evidence through authorised read-only access?
Which control failures have caused actual close delays or audit adjustments?
Who can approve financial control conclusions and who can change configuration?
Do proposed tests assess transaction reliability or introduce employee monitoring?

tasks.short: Prepare and verify Noordhaven’s annual accounts and supporting financial statements.

today.trigger: Year-end close, an audit request or a required financial statement.
steps: Gather the final trial balance, comparative figures and supporting schedules.
Map ledger accounts to statement lines and reconcile totals.
Prepare statements, disclosure schedules and draft accounting notes.
Review estimates, completeness and Dutch reporting requirements with the Controller and auditor.
Resolve review comments and prepare the approved filing package.
systems: Applicable SBR filing software or service
drudgery: Transferring approved figures into reporting templates
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: version control, disclosure completeness and reconciling late adjustments across the accounts and supporting schedules.

lenses.faster: Automated mappings and tie-outs populate figures, while a model drafts notes from approved schedules and policies. For each 60 minutes today, retain 33 minutes for disclosure completeness, estimates, auditor questions and final verification: 45% saved.
lenses.autonomous: An approved year-end trial balance starts statement assembly and note drafting. The Accountant checks every output, and the Controller and required company approvers authorise the final accounts and filing.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give the Controller a quarterly preview of year-end disclosure gaps and missing audit evidence. Demand would grow as preparation becomes cheaper because issues could be resolved before the annual close.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss updating the same cross-references after every adjustment. The Accountant gets more time to assess estimates and explain reporting judgements to the auditor.
lenses.options: Compare supported valuation scenarios and their effects on statements and disclosures. This can change the approved estimate or the evidence requested, while accounting policy limits the available choices.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards coordinating reporting judgements and resolving disclosure gaps. The Accountant gains delegated authority to clear tie-outs and evidence requests, while the Controller approves material judgements; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Controller’s preparation of the annual reporting checklist and audit evidence index after learning Dutch GAAP disclosure requirements and the applicable SBR taxonomy.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant determines whether the statements give a complete and defensible account of the business, including obligations that are absent from ledger balances.
tasks.pattern_why: llm_step: deterministic mappings prepare figures, and a constrained call drafts notes from approved facts; a tie-out and disclosure gate is essential.

in_practice.trigger: The Controller approves the year-end trial balance version for statement preparation.
steps: Map balances to statement lines and run deterministic totals and comparative checks.
Assemble approved schedules, policies and a checklist for the applicable Dutch reporting framework.
Draft notes from those sources, explicitly flagging missing disclosure information.
Have the Accountant verify figures, notes and completeness and resolve auditor questions.
After formal approval, prepare and validate the filing package through the applicable SBR route.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves tie-outs and draft disclosures; the Controller approves accounting judgements, and statutory approvers authorise the accounts and filing.
systems: Applicable SBR filing software or service
data_needed: Approved trial balance and comparative accounts
Statement mappings and disclosure checklist
Approved estimates, policies and supporting schedules
Company size classification, reporting framework and filing requirements
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint annual accounts file with balance versions, mapping checks, note references, approvals and filing validation receipts.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents SBR filing requirements for large companies from financial year 2025 and states that AFAS cannot perform that filing for them.
The broader benchmark does not establish reliable autonomous completion of accounting judgement tasks; it also does not validate Dutch GAAP reporting.

risks: Ledger mappings cannot establish that all required disclosures are present.
Late entries may leave different statement versions inconsistent.
No cited benchmark validates a Dutch annual accounts or statutory audit file.
Noordhaven’s size classification and filing route must be confirmed; AFAS alone may not provide the required submission.
research_questions: Which Dutch reporting framework, company size classification and filing requirements apply?
Are statement mappings and disclosure checklists complete and maintained?
How much time is spent on mechanical preparation versus estimates and auditor questions?
Can every generated note be traced to approved evidence and independently verified?

tasks.short: Check transaction compliance and interview colleagues about gaps in the records.

today.trigger: A scheduled compliance review, transaction exception or audit concern.
steps: Select records and obtain contracts, approvals and transaction evidence.
Check recording, authorisation and the applicable financial or employment-related requirements.
Interview workers and process owners to understand exceptions and actual practice.
Corroborate explanations and document findings.
Agree corrections or escalation and verify follow-up.
drudgery: Turning verified notes into follow-up lists
today.time_sinks: Assumed workflow: collecting records across agencies and sites, arranging shift-friendly interviews and corroborating explanations.

lenses.faster: Deterministic checks prepare exception lists and a copilot organises evidence and interview questions. For each 60 minutes today, retain 42 minutes for interviews, corroboration, judgement and follow-up: 30% saved.
lenses.autonomous: A review schedule starts authorised transaction checks and evidence assembly. The Accountant chooses interview priorities, conducts interviews and approves conclusions; automated flags never become findings by themselves.
lenses.ambitious: New service: offer night-shift supervisors at all three sites a quarterly review of transaction handover and approval problems. Demand would grow as preparation becomes cheaper, although interview and follow-up capacity would still constrain coverage.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching agency portals for the same supporting records. The Accountant gets more time to listen to workers and understand why procedures break down during shifts.
lenses.options: Prepare alternative interview paths for a missing record, unclear responsibility or a system failure. Choosing between them changes which evidence is collected and avoids prematurely treating every exception as misconduct.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts towards evidence-led interviews and practical correction across sites. The Accountant gains delegated authority to request financial evidence and recommend remediation, while HR handles employment consequences and management accepts risk; the work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Payroll Specialist’s preparation of agency-hours-to-invoice exception packs after learning the applicable CAO rates, overtime rules and payroll cut-off conventions.
Absorb the Bookkeeper’s follow-up on missing transaction approvals after learning site approval responsibilities and evidence standards.

tasks.human_edge: The Accountant builds trust in interviews, notices when an explanation conflicts with actual practice and distinguishes an honest process failure from evidence warranting escalation.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: interviews and interpretation remain person-led; deterministic checks and bounded drafting assistance reduce preparation and documentation effort.

in_practice.trigger: The Accountant opens an approved review with a defined scope and lawful access to records.
steps: Run versioned duplicate, approval and agency-hours reconciliation checks over the in-scope records.
Assemble source-linked exception packs and draft neutral interview questions.
Have the Accountant conduct interviews at times accessible to the relevant shifts.
Corroborate explanations against records and draft findings from verified facts.
Approve corrections or escalation and verify completion with the responsible owner.
in_practice.human_gate: The Accountant approves interview scope and every finding; the relevant Finance or HR authority approves consequential action.
data_needed: Transactions, approvals and supporting documents
Agency hours, invoices and relevant contract terms
Applicable CAO rules and approved control definitions
Verified interview notes, access permissions and retention rules
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint review file containing test results, evidence references, verified notes, decisions and remediation status.

evidence.claim: The cited month-end benchmark explicitly excludes communication, asking the right questions and building tacit context.
Rule-based transaction checks can support interviews, but the proposed cross-site workflow and saving have not been demonstrated at Noordhaven.

risks: Duplicate or unusual transactions may have legitimate explanations.
Applying the wrong CAO, period or agency contract can create false exceptions.
Employee records and interview notes require restricted access and AVG-compliant retention.
If the design introduces employee monitoring or employment decisions, assess OR involvement and EU AI Act requirements before extending its scope.
research_questions: Are agency hours, invoice lines and approval records detailed enough for reproducible tests?
Which CAO and agency contract rules apply to each worker category and period?
Can interviews reach night shifts and flex workers without disrupting operations?
Does the intended scope remain financial compliance, or introduce employee monitoring or employment decisions?

role.altitude: The Accountant becomes a financial evidence and exception specialist: reviewing reproducible workpapers, resolving valuation and tax questions, and helping sites prevent issues that delay close. Delegated rights can cover clearing routine reconciliations, requesting evidence and escalating material exceptions; material judgements, filing and payments retain their designated approvers.
reach: FP&A Analyst: first-pass site variance explanations and investment scenarios, after learning operational drivers and forecasting models.
Controller: audit action tracking, reporting checklists and control-test preparation, after learning materiality, Dutch reporting requirements and escalation standards.
Credit and Collections Officer: provision-review evidence preparation, after learning dispute and collection histories.
Payroll Specialist and Bookkeeper: agency invoice exception preparation and missing-approval follow-up, after learning CAO rules, contract terms and cut-offs.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 415 hours per FTE annually, about 26% of a 1,600-hour year. The proposed savings release about 380 hours across both Accountants, worth about EUR 26,600 of capacity at EUR 70/hour; workflows and savings are hypotheses, and this is not a cash saving or an estimate for the remaining role. Interviews, difficult judgements, poor source data and approval responsibilities limit further automation.
skills_to_grow: Build and validate reproducible Excel or SQL reconciliations with versioned inputs.
Maintain AFAS mappings, reporting snapshots and financial control tests.
Check model-generated workpapers against evidence and identify unsupported assumptions.
Develop Dutch GAAP, tax, CAO and agency-contract knowledge within the role’s remit.
Conduct neutral interviews and explain financial consequences to site managers.
Apply access controls, AVG requirements and change governance to financial workflows.
role.ambitious_version: Provide the Controller and all three site managers with earlier, evidence-backed warnings about close blockers, tax cash needs and control failures. Start with reconciliations and reporting drafts, then expand only where measured review effort falls and audit adjustments do not rise; use the released capacity to improve forecast inputs and resolve operational causes before month end.
